questions.text: A teammate misunderstands your instructions on a group project. What's your first move?

options.label: Re-explain calmly and check they understood
Write it down step-by-step so there's no ambiguity
Ask them what part was confusing before re-explaining
Take over that part yourself to save time

questions.text: You have three deadlines in the same week. How do you usually handle it?

options.label: Make a list and tackle the most urgent first
Work on all three a little each day
Focus fully on one at a time, finish, then move on
Start with whichever feels easiest to build momentum

questions.text: Listen to the scenario, then choose how you'd respond to the client.

options.label: Be upfront about the delay and give a new timeline
Reassure them first, explain the details after
Loop your teammate in immediately so they hear it too
Ask your team lead to handle the client conversation

questions.text: You're given a task with unclear instructions. What do you do first?

options.label: Ask clarifying questions before starting
Make reasonable assumptions and start, adjusting later
Research similar past examples for guidance
Break the task into smaller parts to understand it

questions.text: Click the spot in the room where you'd naturally position yourself during a group project.
A group project is falling behind. What's your instinct?

options.label: Step up and reorganize the plan for everyone
Check in with each person individually first
Suggest a quick group meeting to realign
Focus on finishing your own part well, as an example

questions.text: It's 9pm and you haven't started an assignment due tomorrow. What now?

options.label: Start immediately and push through
Quickly plan what's essential vs. skippable, then start
Get a full night's sleep and wake up early instead
Message classmates to see how far along they are

questions.text: You solve a problem, but later realize a flaw in your solution. What do you do?

options.label: Fix it immediately, even if it means starting over
Patch the flaw without redoing the whole thing
Analyze why you missed it, then fix it
Ask someone else to review before changing anything
